items.sentence: The flesh is firm and juicy, surrounding a central core that holds several small, dark seeds.
A thin skin encloses pale flesh, with color varying among cultivars from green through yellow to deep red.
Most varieties have a rounded shape, often narrowing slightly toward the stem and blossom ends.
These fruits grow on deciduous trees in the rose family, whose branches bear clusters of blossoms.
After harvest, its flesh can turn brown when cut surfaces react with oxygen through enzymatic oxidation.
During ripening, the fruit releases ethylene, a plant hormone that can accelerate softening in nearby produce.
Bees and other insects transfer pollen among blossoms, enabling fertilization and subsequent fruit development.
As it ripens, starch reserves convert into sugars, increasing sweetness while acidity often decreases.
Commercial orchards often grow trees in rows, with pruning and thinning used to manage light and crop load.
Trees are cultivated across temperate regions, where winter chilling supports reliable flowering in many varieties.
Harvest typically takes place in late summer or autumn, although timing varies with cultivar and local climate.
Cool, humid storage environments help preserve firmness after picking, while controlled atmospheres extend storage life.
Fresh slices provide dietary fiber, especially when the edible skin is left intact.
The fruit is pressed to produce juice and fermented to make cider in regions with established traditions.
Pectin from its tissues helps set jams and jellies during cooking.
Orchard blossoms supply nectar and pollen for insects early in the growing season.
